The interface tweaks worth knowing
Premium & Safety · September 26, 2026 · 3 min read · Fast Scheduler team

Telegram is the most customizable mainstream messenger, and almost nobody touches the settings that matter. Beyond the dark-mode toggle lives a theme editor, per-chat wallpapers, folder systems and interface tweaks that change daily usability. The full tour:
The quick toggle
— Settings → Appearance → theme, or the sun/moon icon. It follows the system automatically if set to "Auto".
The deep version — the theme editor.

Tap any theme's edit button and Telegram exposes every color in the interface: backgrounds, text, accents, the unread badge. "Create New Theme" clones the current one for editing. This is where channel owners make dark mode theirs: a custom accent matching the channel's brand color makes every screenshot you share subtly branded.
Dark mode done right is AMOLED dark.
The pattern/gradient backgrounds look nice on LCD; on OLED phones, the pure-black theme saves real battery. The theme editor can set true #000000 backgrounds.
Telegram Folders (Settings → Folders) split the chat list into tabbed workspaces: Work, Channels, Unread, Family. The power configs:
A "Channels" folder
holding only channels — your reading list separated from conversations. Combined with "Exclude Muted", the tab shows only channels with unread content: a self-cleaning reading queue.
An "Unread" folder
with "Include: Unread only" — every unread chat across all accounts in one tab.
Folders sync across devices
and can be shared via invite links — a curated folder of niche channels is itself shareable content (channels use this: "our starter pack of 20 quality channels").
Custom wallpaper per chat:
any chat's background can be set individually — a different wallpaper for the channel-ops chat vs family is how power users navigate by color.
Pattern wallpapers:
Telegram generates subtle patterns from any color combination; the dark-mode trick is a dark base with a low-opacity pattern for depth without brightness.
Animated backgrounds
exist but cost battery and attention — the honest recommendation is solid or pattern.
Message text size
is independent of system font size (Appearance slider) — set it once, globally.
"Change number" vs "Add account":
up to three accounts on one app, each with its own notification profile.
Chat list density
and the archive function: archiving noisy but needed chats beats leaving them in the main list.
Built-in "Power saving" mode
(newer versions) tames animations and autoplay — pairs well with the AMOLED theme.
For channel owners specifically, one UI habit matters beyond aesthetics: running the app in
both light and dark
and checking your channel's avatar, emoji and post formatting in each. Half your audience sees dark; branding that only works in light is half-broken.
Common questions
How do I force Telegram into true black (AMOLED) dark mode?

Settings → Appearance → Dark theme, then edit the theme and set the background colors to pure black (#000000), or pick a community AMOLED theme. True black saves battery on OLED screens compared to the default dark-gray.
What are Telegram chat folders and how do I set them up?
Folders (Settings → Folders) are tabbed filters for your chat list — e.g. a Channels-only tab, an Unread tab, a Work tab. They sync across devices and can be shared via invite links.
Can I use a different wallpaper for each chat?
Yes — open any chat, tap its name, then "Change wallpaper". Each chat can have its own background, including custom colors and patterns, independent of the global theme.
